definition: The initial phase of training a language model on a large, general-purpose text corpus before any task-specific fine-tuning.
details: Pretraining is where a model acquires broad linguistic, factual, and reasoning knowledge, typically using a self-supervised objective like next-token prediction, and requires the vast majority of the total compute used to build an LLM.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Pretraining.
